subject: PrivStack: module contract + simulated deploy plan
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PrivStack: module contract + simulated deploy plan

Hey Vanessa / Naomi,

I sketched a short tabletop + simulated deploy we want to run next week against the Acme staging cluster to validate the module contracts for the VPC shard and the Helm/Ansible glue. The goal is to catch interface mismatches (IPAM, subnet allocation, servicecidr collisions) and CI gating gaps before we run any live provisioning.

High level plan attached (sim-deploy-plan.md) — it contains:
- a sequence-of-steps for a dry-run deploy (Terraform plan, Helm template, Ansible converge)
- a list of invariants the infra tests must assert (mtu, host routes, SR-IOV annotations, BGP next-hops)
- expected failure modes and rollback indicators

Ask: can you both review the module contract diffs I attached (module-contracts.diff) and flag any hard-coded CIDR or provider assumptions? If we can get this back by Monday EOD I’ll schedule the simulated run with Acme.

For traceability I added a JIRA ticket (JIRA-PRIV-4821) and a CI job stub (see related links).

Thanks,
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, infra-team@acme.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrivStack: module contract + simulated deploy plan

Thanks Mateo — skimmed the plan and the diffs. A few immediate items:

- IPAM: the Terraform module still assumes a /16 allocation for tenant subnets. That collides with Acme's current allocation; recommend adding a "cidr_policy" variable with explicit deny-list for known ranges.
- BGP & multi-home: Helm values don't expose AS path prepend or next-hop override. If Acme uses a dual-spine WAN we should avoid implicit default gateway assumptions.
- MTU & SR-IOV: add an explicit mtu override for the host-interface role and make SR-IOV annotations optional behind a flag; some of Acme's edge hosts do not support VF drivers in staging.
- CI gating: the CI job should fail-fast on any Terraform plan that introduces state drift for subnets. Right now the job only runs plan without a guard.

I'll inline small diffs in the module-contracts.diff and share a quick patch by EOD.

Cc'ing Karthik for network validation automation — Karthik, can you run the network-sim against the provided kubevirt topology and confirm the host route expectations?

- Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ops Lead <ops-lead@acme.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: infra-team@acme.com
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrivStack: module contract + simulated deploy plan

Thanks Mateo — Acme infra team is available next Wednesday (2026-09-23) for the simulated run window. A few notes from our side:

- We'll provide a small staging VPC with reserved /20 for the test. Please ensure the plan can accept a provider-supplied base CIDR.
- Our staging hosts have mixed NICs; SR-IOV is off by default.
- We can supply a read-only copy of the BGP config used in prod so you can mirror next-hop behavior.

I uploaded a snapshot of the staging kubevirt layout here: https://acme.example.com/staging-layout-20260920 (shared with the infra-team contact).

If you want us to run any pre-check scripts on our side let us know — we can run an MTU sweep and report back.

—Chris
Chris Delgado
Ops Lead, Acme Industrial

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, ops-lead@acme.com
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrivStack: module contract + simulated deploy plan

Folks — thanks Chris and Vanessa. Quick consolidation and next steps:

1) Variable updates (owner: Mateo / Vanessa) — we’ll add a cidr_policy variable and mtu_override to the terraform/host module. Mateo will open a tiny patch and request review by EOD.
2) CI gating (owner: Naomi) — Naomi, can you add the plan-fail-on-subnet-drift check into the privstack CI job? Ideally the job should run terraform plan + validate outputs against a saved golden netmap.
3) Network sim (owner: Karthik) — Karthik to run the network-sim against Acme's staging snapshot and attach results (network-sim-output.txt) to the JIRA ticket.
4) Schedule (owner: Mateo) — I’ll book a 2-hour window with Acme for 2026-09-23 09:00-11:00 PT for the simulated run; goal is non-destructive plan -> helm template -> ansible converge dry-run.

Attach: sim-deploy-plan.md, module-contracts.diff
Related links: https://drive.redwood.com/privstack/sim-deploy-plan, JIRA-PRIV-4821

If no objections I’ll push the cidr_policy patch and move the CI job into a gated pipeline so the sim run is gated by the plan checks.

Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrivStack: module contract + simulated deploy plan

All good from CI side — I’ll add the terraform plan drift guard and a smoke test that validates the golden netmap. I also pushed a small helper script to the repo that will compare the planned subnet allocations to the allowed ranges and exit non-zero if there is overlap.

I will attach the CI job logs and the smoke-test results to JIRA-PRIV-4821 after the simulated run completes. If Acme runs an MTU sweep before Wednesday, please send the output and I’ll fold it into the preflight validations.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
SRE, Redwood Inference
